name: Caryā (Śaiva temple service)
method_summary: Service of Śiva in the temple with the body: sweeping and smearing the floor, gathering flowers and making garlands, lighting lamps, singing the hymns, serving devotees — in the attitude of a servant (dāsa-mārga), as Appar did.
signs_of_progress: the fruit is sālokya, dwelling in Śiva's world

name: Kriyā (Śaiva ritual worship)
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the liṅga or image with the prescribed mantras, offerings and fire — the son's attitude (satputra-mārga), as Campantar's.

name: Yoga (Śivayoga)
method_summary: Inner worship and meditation on Śiva: the Āgamas' six-limbed yoga (breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, reasoning [tarka], absorption) or the Tirumantiram's eight limbs, fixing the mind on Śiva in the heart or at the centres — the friend's attitude (sakhā-mārga), as Cuntarar's.

warnings.text: The powers that arise from yoga are not the goal; only knowledge by grace gives final release.

name: Jñāna (knowledge of Śiva)
method_summary: Knowledge given by grace through the guru, cultivated in four steps: hearing (kēṭṭal), reflecting (cintittal), clarity (teḷital) and abiding (niṭṭai); seeing the tattvas and the soul as not-Śiva and the world as a mirage, meditating the five letters, abiding at Śiva's feet — the true path (san-mārga).

name: Dīkṣā (Śaiva initiation)
method_summary: The guru, having become Śiva by ritual identification, removes or burns the disciple's bonds by mantra-power (Sanskrit manuals), or initiates by look, touch, word, thought, scripture, yoga or fire (Tamil).

name: Samaya-dīkṣā
method_summary: The first initiation, conferring the status of samayin with rules of conduct and the right to worship and study.

name: Viśeṣa-dīkṣā
method_summary: The 'special' initiation that qualifies the initiate for the regular worship of Śiva (content varies among manuals).

name: Nirvāṇa-dīkṣā
method_summary: The liberating initiation: the guru purifies the six paths in the disciple and burns the bonds; with 'seed' the initiate keeps the post-initiatory rules, 'seedless' for those unable to; liberation follows at the fall of the body.

name: Consecration as ācārya or sādhaka
method_summary: Ācāryābhiṣeka empowers an initiate to initiate and teach; sādhakābhiṣeka empowers one who seeks powers (bubhukṣu) to master a mantra.

name: Ātmārtha-pūjā (daily private worship of Śiva)
method_summary: The initiate's daily worship: bath with water and ash, twilight rites, bhūtaśuddhi, nyāsa, inner worship, worship of the liṅga with the five brahma-mantras and six limb-mantras, fire offering and japa.

name: Parārtha-pūjā (temple worship)
method_summary: Worship performed for others in the temple by consecrated Ādiśaiva priests.

name: Antaryāga (inner worship)
method_summary: Worship of Śiva in the heart with mental offerings before or instead of outer worship; the Tirumantiram makes the heart the sanctum and the soul the liṅga.

name: Bhūtaśuddhi
method_summary: Purification of the elements of the body by meditation and mantra before worship.

name: Nyāsa
method_summary: Installing the brahma- and limb-mantras on the hands and body so that the worshipper becomes Śiva for the worship.

name: Agnikārya (Śaiva fire rite)
method_summary: Offerings into a consecrated fire in which Śiva is invoked, part of daily worship and of dīkṣā.

name: Mahotsava (great temple festival)
method_summary: The annual festival: flag-hoisting, processions of the deity, and the concluding bath.

name: Repetition of the five syllables (namaccivāya)
method_summary: Repeating and meditating na-ma-śi-vā-ya (or śivāya namaḥ) — aloud, softly or mentally — as refuge and as the means of purification; Tamil Siddhānta teaches the letters' meaning so that the soul turns toward grace.
prerequisites: in Siddhānta teaching, received from the guru

name: Singing the Tirumuṟai (paṇṇicai)
method_summary: Singing the Tēvāram and other Tirumuṟai hymns in their melodic modes during temple worship and at home; the ōtuvār's office.

name: Wearing the sacred ash and rudrākṣa
method_summary: Smearing tirunīṟu (in three horizontal lines) and wearing rudrākṣa beads as the marks of Śiva's devotee; praised as mantra and medicine.

name: Worship and service of devotees (Māhēśvara-pūjā)
method_summary: Feeding, serving and honouring Śiva's devotees as Śiva himself; the freed soul's conduct (Civañāṉa Pōtam 12) and the practice of many Nāyaṉmārs.

name: Mental temple-building and worship
method_summary: Building and consecrating a temple entirely in the mind and worshipping Śiva there, as Pūcalār and Vāyilār did.

equivalents.note: inner worship as a sustained practice rather than a ritual segment

name: Pilgrimage to the Tēvāram shrines
method_summary: Visiting and singing at the shrines praised in the Tēvāram (the 274 'sung places', pāṭal peṟṟa talam) and at Chidambaram, following the saints' journeys.

name: The Mārkaḻi dawn vow (Tiruvempāvai nōṉpu)
method_summary: In the month of Mārkaḻi, rising before dawn, bathing and singing the Tiruvempāvai and Tiruppaḷḷiyeḻucci.

name: Tirumūlar's eightfold yoga
method_summary: Tirumūlar's eight limbs — restraints, observances, posture, breath control, withdrawal, holding, meditation, absorption — taught to preserve the body as the vessel of realization and to reach Śiva within; summary only.

warnings.text: Breath retention and advanced practices are to be learned only from a guru (general teaching of the text; specific verses not recorded here).

name: Pariyaṅka yōkam
method_summary: A yoga of the third tantra of the Tirumantiram involving union with a consort; recorded as a name and summary only.

warnings.text: Restricted practice: no method recorded. The text places it within guru-directed yoga (specific warnings not verified).

name: Non-killing (kollāmai)
method_summary: Refraining from taking any life and protecting all creatures, even at the cost of one's own life.

name: Abstaining from meat (pulāl maṟuttal)
method_summary: Refusing flesh food, praised above a thousand sacrifices.

name: Hospitality (viruntōmpal)
method_summary: Receiving and feeding guests as the purpose of the householder's life.

name: Austerity (tavam)
method_summary: Enduring pain and harming none (Kuṟaḷ ch. 27).
